entities.name: Panthéon-Assas University Paris
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Panthéon-Assas University Paris, established in 1971, is a prominent public research university located in the Latin Quarter of Paris, France. It emerged from the legacy of the University of Paris, specifically focusing on law and political science, fields that are critical to understanding the structure of modern governance. As an institution, it serves as a nexus for legal education, influencing not only French law but also European legal systems through its rigorous academic programs and notable alumni, including politicians, judges, and scholars who have shaped contemporary France.

Since its inception, Panthéon-Assas has been pivotal in developing specialized legal disciplines, hosting significant conferences, and producing influential research that has informed legal practice and policy. The university's curriculum emphasizes a mix of theoretical and practical approaches, preparing students to engage with the complexities of the legal landscape. Its facilities and resources have attracted students from around the globe, fostering a diverse intellectual environment that supports international legal dialogue and collaboration.

The legacy of Panthéon-Assas extends beyond its academic contributions; it has played a key role in the evolution of legal frameworks and civil rights discussions in France and Europe. The university has produced a significant number of legal practitioners who have influenced both national legislation and international law, thus perpetuating its impact through generations. Moreover, its focus on law and political science has contributed to a broader understanding of the interplay between legal systems and social justice in contemporary society.
